subject: Mid-term capacity uplift & rebalance credit request
messages:
From: Sophia Tan <sophia.tan@mlopslabs.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: procure@mlopslabs.com
Date: Fri, 20 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Mid-term capacity uplift & rebalance credit request

Hi Mina / Karthik,

Thanks again for the great Q2 check-in last week. We had an unexpected production ramp for our conversational moderation model — sustained traffic spike for approximately 8–10 weeks starting late April. Our current Dedicated pool (32 A100-equivalent GPUs) handles baseline load fine, but we need to add capacity for 60–90 days to maintain the 95th percentile latency target (<120ms).

Request: can Redwood support a mid-term uplift of +8 GPUs for 90 days and provide a partial credit/rebalance against our existing commit rather than charging full burst rates? Procurement is sensitive to one-off burst spend and prefers to see any uplift amortized, or at least discounted, against the annual commit.

Concrete numbers we need:
- Option A: Short-term burst (exact cost and SLA for +8 GPUs for 90 days)
- Option B: Mid-term reserved amendment (add 8 GPUs to the commit, pro rata pricing and amortization schedule)
- Any credit we could apply for moving part of projected burst usage into the existing commitment pool (we have ~6 unused months on the current term)

I attached our internal note with traffic projections and the signed PO for context. Can you outline realistic commercial options and timelines for an amendment? We need internal approval by 2028-04-27.

Best,
Sophia Tan
Head of Platform Reliability
MLOps Labs

Attachments: MLOpsLabs_Midterm_Request_20280420.pdf (3 pages: traffic graphs, PO stub)

From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.ai>
To: Sophia Tan <sophia.tan@mlopslabs.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Apr 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mid-term capacity uplift & rebalance credit request

Hi Sophia — thanks for the context and the traffic snapshot. Short answer: yes, we have two practical paths and a hybrid that customers use frequently. High-level options below; I put rough commercials to help procurement compare quickly.

Option 1 — Temporary burst (fast, no contract change):
- +8 GPUs for 90 days as a burst allocation, billed at our short-term rate: $3,000 / GPU / month.
- Total delta ~ $3,000 * 8 * 3 = $72,000.
- No change to committed pool; throughput/latency SLO maintained by routing to burst nodes with identical configuration.
- Good if you want immediate capacity and no legal/PO changes.

Option 2 — Mid-term reserved amendment (preferred for $/month):
- Add 8 GPUs to the reserved commit. We can apply a mid-term amendment with a discounted reserved rate of $1,950 / GPU / month (10% off list for mid-term adds).
- Delta ~ $1,950 * 8 = $15,600 / month. If you amortize over remaining 12 months (we can also do 9–12mo options), procurement sees a lower monthly impact.
- We can issue a pro rata credit for any overlapping months of unused commit. Example: if you have 6 unused months on the original commit, we can calculate a credit that reduces the first 6 amortized payments.

Option 3 — Hybrid (burst + commit conversion):
- Immediate +8 burst for 30–60 days at burst rate, then convert the uplift to reserved commit for the remaining period with a credit equal to X% of burst fees (we typically credit 30–50% of burst spend if converted to reserved within 90 days).

Next steps I need from your side to produce a formal amendment and numbers:
1) Confirm preferred path (1/2/3) or ask us to recommend based on traffic curve.
2) Confirm whether procurement needs an amortization window (9/12/24 months).
3) Any contracting constraints for a short amendment (PO number, billing entity).

I’m looping in Marissa (acct exec) to draft the amendment and DocuSign. Karthik — can you flag any quota/SLA caveats for adding 8 GPUs mid-term (networking, licensing)?

Thanks — Mina
Director, Customer Growth 
Redwood Inference

Thanks Mina. Quick technical notes for Sophia:
- We can guarantee the same model performance on burst nodes, but for throughput guarantees tied to route-level SLOs we recommend a 48–72 hour warm-up window for KV cache population if you use heavy prefix reuse. Expect transient 95th pctl latency variance during warmup.
- No additional networking setup required if you keep the same VPC peering config; we’ll schedule capacity in the same region.
- If you plan to convert burst -> reserved, tag the burst requests with your account and traffic identifier so logs count toward conversion credit thresholds.

If you’re comfortable with the business options Mina outlined, Marissa will send a draft amendment for legal/finance.

— Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Sophia — attaching a proposed amendment and two commercial layouts for procurement to review (attached). Highlights:
- Path A (Burst 90d): +8 GPUs at $3,000/GPU/mo; bill monthly; no contract change.
- Path B (Amend +8 GPUs): $1,950/GPU/mo; we amortize new capacity over remaining 12 months by default; first 3 months include a pro rata credit equivalent to unused months on existing commitment (example included in doc).
- Conversion credit: if you take Path A now and convert within 60 days, we apply a 40% credit on burst spend toward the amendment.

I created a draft DocuSign envelope with the amendment for Path B (if you want the reserved approach). Link: https://www.docusign.com/sign/EXAMPLE-ID-20280423 (also in related links).

Requested response by EOD 2028-04-27 so procurement can route the PO. If you want a faster temporary lift while we finalize amendment, we can stand up burst capacity within 24 hours after PO confirmation.

Attachments: Redwood_Proposed_Amendment_20280423.docx

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Thanks team — appreciate the clear options. Procurement prefers Path B (amend +8 GPUs) but asks two clarifications before we sign:
1) Please show the pro rata credit calculation using our remaining 6 months of unused commitment in the amendment (line item).
2) We want a written SLA note that the new capacity will meet our 95th pctl latency target and that Redwood will provide a one-time credit if the latency target is missed for more than 48 hours cumulatively in the first 30 days after uplift.

If you can incorporate those and send an updated DocuSign, we’ll aim to route the PO the same day.

Best,
Sophia
